## Historical audit — S0070, chunk 1 of 5

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_probes/C1/selection/commons_133800864/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. Only the supplied chunk was examined; neither image is visible to this audit.

**Goal versus evidence:** The assigned goal was an editable, photograph-matched indoor reconstruction, including perspective, objects, materials and placement (student request, line 1). The student interpreted it as a kitchen corner; object labels and estimated anchors are the student’s interpretation, not independent verification of the photograph.

| Evidence | Observed operation or result |
|---|---|
| Student response, lines 3 and 6 | Produced a nonempty SceneAct program with separate architecture, blinds, cabinet, paper holder, towel and ring, sink, jug, pitcher, blender and smaller objects. It specifies folded towel geometry, tilted pitcher lid and blender cup, shared counter elevation, colored materials, noise/bump textures, metallic shaders, camera, world and lights. Grouping and intended supports do not establish physical contact or visual correctness. |
| Student request line 4; response line 6 | A **source-audit instruction**, not an identified teacher diagnosis, stated that the draft had not run and requested checks for radii, endpoints, keys, grouping and material isolation. The subsequent program adopted assertions and helpers, separated cup and sponge assets, narrowed paper-texture targeting, and conditionally initialized the world. No separately identified teacher input or teacher detection is visible. |
| Execute line 7; execution result line 8, characters [0,118670); select line 9 | Step 1 was executed; the runner reported `ok: true`, a completed render and saved image and blend file, and selected step 1. This is execution/render success, not a formal visual, geometric or editability pass. |
| Student request line 10, characters [0,161270); response line 12 | Reference and render were supplied for comparison. The student reported narrow window coverage, right-cropped roll and jug, absent pitcher, and low counter/towel; these are student observations, not independently checked here. It hypothesized narrow framing and excessive rightward spacing. |
| Student response line 12; execute line 13 | The revision changed lens 80 to 62 and shifted roll, jug and pitcher left while retaining camera pose and lighting. The revised program was executed as step 2; its result is outside this visible chunk. |

**Exploration and outcome.** Within the visible trace the student made its own inventory, estimated anchors and camera, compared the supplied render, and proposed both global and local explanations. The first two CLI sessions reported no tool calls (lines 2 and 5); the comparison session likewise reported none (line 11). No diagnostic probes were available. The visible outcome is a successful first build/render and a launched second build; final selection, formal success, partial correctness, algorithm failure, empty patch or interruption cannot be determined from this chunk.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferable: executable validation and visual correspondence are different claims; grouping, explicit checks and isolated material copies support a testable editable build but do not prove connections. Task-specific: the chosen kitchen inventory, 80-to-62 lens change and leftward moves respond to this student’s reported framing. Whether the pitcher was out of frame or occluded, whether supports actually connect, whether transparency and textures look right, and whether camera or local spacing caused the reported discrepancies remain unresolved. Changing lens and positions together prevents attributing any later improvement to either alone.
